non_promotion_rule: A systematic-uncertainty row is a loss/cap object. It prevents model, detector, survey, proof, benchmark, foreground, and nuisance uncertainty from being hidden inside a likelihood/update row.

systematic_rows.uncertainty_source: identifier drift, version ambiguity, provenance gaps, mutable repository pointers, and generated-summary mismatch
systematic_rows.bias_or_failure_mode: metadata defects can falsely imply replayability or publicness while adding no physical support.
systematic_rows.nuisance_parameters: repository version, checksum, provenance graph, agent/activity/entity records, license/access state, and package identity.
systematic_rows.stress_test: reconstruct the carrier/protocol chain from metadata alone and compare checksums/generated summaries; if not possible, demote to non-spendable custody warning.
systematic_rows.mitigation_or_bound: freeze version metadata, include provenance graph, record checksums, and distinguish custody repair from evidence update.
systematic_rows.residual_effect: metadata residuals affect custody only and cannot promote any route above S0 by themselves.
systematic_rows.authority_spend_rule: For multi-route rows, this row-level S-field is a family-level envelope only; route-spendable credit is limited by route_authority_ceilings and the route state ledger.
